POSE.md:1078:**Accepted limits.** A spec may declare the residual limits of its guarantees under `### Accepted limits`, one `- L<N>: <assumption>. Accepted because <reason>.` per limit; `lint-spec --ready-check` refuses a limit that does not say why it is accepted, and, when an ADR cites the spec, one the ADR does not name. The review plan and the bundle seal the limits (`accepted_limits`, part of the plan digest; in a scope with several specs each id is qualified as `<spec>#L<N>`), and the brief of template `review-brief/11` lists them: a finding that falls inside one is a follow-up with `limit` set to its id, recorded in the attestation with disposition `within-limit`, which does not block an approval whatever its severity; a limit the bundle did not seal, or a `within-limit` finding without a reason, is refused. A reviewer who finds a limit unjustified reports a finding that disputes it, which blocks as any finding does. A review converges by classifying what was declared out of scope, not by a cap on rounds.
POSE.md:1082:**Delegated-review requests.** `pose review request <scope|bundle> --kind delegated-review [--purpose review|adjudicate|smoke] [--agents <name,...>] [--note-file <path>] [--apply]` opens an action request of kind `delegated-review` that binds the project, the worktree, the scope, the sealed bundle, the brief, the notes, the policies, the accepted agents and the destination of the conclusion (an attestation, an adjudication record or smoke evidence). No actor answers it: `pose action fulfil <act-id> --run <run-id> --runner agent:<id> --idempotency-key <key> --expected-revision <n> [--channel cli|ci|conductor] [--envelope <file>] [--apply]`, or the MCP tool `pose_action_fulfil`, submits a completed run, and the engine records the fulfilment only when the run is of the request's brief and bundle, of an accepted agent, completed with its containment, its signed proof verifies, its attempt ledger is intact and the engine recorded its conclusion at the request's destination; the fulfilment is verified again on every read. `pose delegate review <scope> --request <act-id>` runs the request's brief locally and submits the run once concluded. A rejecting run fulfils the request without approving anything; a superseded bundle or changed policy invalidates it, even once fulfilled, and it is asked again with `--supersedes <act-id>`, which retires it under the supersession authority rules (`--authority <json>`, `--role <role>`, `--requested-at` from the preview), or, when the plan now reserves the review for a person, makes the person's escalation its successor; a retry with the same key and run is a no-op. A person is asked by exception, as a decision request to the maintainer role: a plan that reserves the review for a person, a spent attempt budget, reviewers in conflict, and a `business_decision` a reviewer raised in its draft. A run's proof verifies in any checkout of the project: the worktree it ran in is recorded, not required of the reader, so a CI job or the Conductor fulfils the request with the same envelope.
